title: Which tasks call for embeddings or an LLM?
prompt: Cartwheel's data team has six requests. Select every one where **embeddings or an LLM** is a better first tool than a classic scikit-learn model on the existing tables.
hints: Ask what the input is: a table of facts, or free text?
Ask what the output is: a calibrated number, or text or similarity?
Three requests involve free text; the other three are tabular or are experiments.
explanation: Searching reviews by meaning, turning ticket text into a topic feature, and summarising reviews are all text problems: embeddings handle the first two cheaply, and an LLM is the natural tool for a written summary a person will read. Forecasting refunds and scoring churn are tabular predictions where scikit-learn gives cheap, testable, calibrated outputs. The coupon question is an experiment to analyse, not a prediction task at all.

review-search.text: Let staff type "arrived broken" and find product reviews that describe damage in any wording.
review-search.why: Good fit: embeddings + nearest-neighbour search match meaning, not exact words.

refund-forecast.text: Forecast next month's refund amount from order and return tables.
refund-forecast.why: Tabular regression with numeric history; a scikit-learn model (with a time-based split) fits.

ticket-topic-feature.text: Turn free-text support tickets into a 'complaint topic' column to test as a churn feature.
ticket-topic-feature.why: Good fit: embed the tickets, cluster or classify them, then let cross-validation judge the new column.

llm-churn-score.text: Ask a chat model to rate each customer's churn risk from their eight numeric columns.
llm-churn-score.why: The labelled table already supports a cheaper, calibrated, testable model; the LLM adds cost and uncertainty.

review-summary.text: Write a one-paragraph weekly summary of new product reviews for the merchandising team.
review-summary.why: Good fit: generating readable text from text is what LLMs do; a person reviews the result.

coupon-ab.text: Decide whether the SPRING15 coupon increased order value, using a randomised test.
coupon-ab.why: That's experiment analysis (compare groups, check significance), not a modelling problem for an LLM.
